document_title: One Rock, Two Readings of the Kenai Loop Gas Storage Lease
post_copy:
Under Kenai's airport, ownership changes once, then splits.

The city owns the surface. The state got the oil and gas estate by federal patent on August 25th, 1986.

ENSTAR and Hilcorp want the Kenai Loop sands 8,600 to 10,500 feet below sea level for gas storage. By DNR's count Hilcorp gave about one quarter of the requested data and no dynamic model like ENSTAR's. DNR found ENSTAR's 3.9 Bcf estimate of gas left more reliable than Hilcorp's 6.4 and preliminarily favors ENSTAR. Evidence was the right test.

DNR asserts clear state authority over the pore space. City Manager Terry Eubank says Kenai owns it, on a Pioneer Law opinion. No model settles a deed.

Nothing is leased yet. Comments are due 5 p.m. November 13th.

Both estimates, each side's evidence, both plans and the pore space claim.

Will Kenai Loop store gas before the deed fight reaches court?

#Kenai #CookInlet #PoreSpace

slides.headline: One rock. Two readings.
slides.body: The state backed the one with the data.
labels: ILLUSTRATION · INTERVAL TO SCALE, OVERBURDEN BROKEN

slides.headline: Same reservoir. Two estimates of the gas left.
slides.body: ENSTAR put the gas left at 3.9 Bcf. Hilcorp said 6.4. The state found ENSTAR's figure more reliable and favors ENSTAR's storage lease.
labels: ORIGINAL GAS IN PLACE, 32.5 BCF, PER DNR

slides.headline: Two sands, sealed in coal.
slides.body: The gas sits in the pores of these sands. The state and the City of Kenai each claim that pore space.
labels: ILLUSTRATION · LAYERS EXPLODED, THICKNESS TO SCALE

slides.headline: The state judged what each company showed it.
slides.body: ENSTAR gave DNR a dynamic reservoir model. DNR says Hilcorp provided about one quarter of the requested data and no model. Hilcorp couldn't comment before Alaska Public Media's story.
labels: HILCORP · ABOUT ONE QUARTER OF THE DATA, PER DNR
ILLUSTRATION · HILCORP HALF DRAWN SOLID IN PROPORTION TO THE DATA PROVIDED, PER DNR

slides.headline: Two plans for one field.
labels: three existing, up to six more
150 MMscf a day at nine wells, roughly 30% at first
28 to 33 Bcf claimed, later "significantly reduced," never amended
NONE OF IT IS BUILT · NOTHING IS LEASED YET

slides.body: ENSTAR says it could fall 18 days short of gas this winter, depending on temperatures.
labels: PER ALASKA PUBLIC MEDIA · NO LEASE IS FINAL YET

slides.headline: Cook Inlet peaked at 196 Bcf in 2006. In-state demand is about 70 now.
slides.body: DNR projects production below demand in the early 2030s. Hilcorp told legislators nearly all of the roughly 30 Bcf it holds in Pool 6 is committed to ENSTAR.
labels: AS MANY AS 15 DATA CENTER PROPOSALS IN ALASKA, PER ALASKA PUBLIC MEDIA NO SOURCE TIES ONE TO KENAI LOOP

slides.headline: The model reads the rock. It can't read the deed.
slides.body: DNR asserts the state has clear authority over the pore space. Kenai's city manager wrote that the city owns it, citing Pioneer Law, and warned of "conflicting leases."
labels: CITY OF KENAI · PIONEER LAW OPINION

slides.headline: Comment to DNR by 5 p.m. November 13th.
slides.body: The finding is preliminary. The Director decides after reading the comments.

editor_notes_for_email: This is a PRELIMINARY finding (C01, C55). Nothing is leased, and the Director decides only after comments close at 5 p.m. November 13th. In replies say 'favors' or 'preliminarily chose', never 'awarded' or 'won'.

Pore space. DNR's 'clear authority' (C47) is a disputed legal assertion and always travels with the City of Kenai's Pioneer Law position (C57). Neither the Eubank letter nor the opinion was fetched; the city's claim reaches the deck through Alaska Public Media (C56, C57).

Every Hilcorp-critical point (one quarter of the data, no dynamic model, the 3.9 vs 6.4 Bcf call) is DNR's characterization. Hilcorp couldn't comment before the October 16th story (C67). Answer pushback with the finding's pages 15 to 16.
No link from Kenai Loop to AI or data centers beyond slide 07's context line, which says no source ties one to the field. ENSTAR's dynamic reservoir model is a physics simulation, not AI.
'18 days short' is ENSTAR's conditional claim relayed by Alaska Public Media (C64). July's RCA order on ENSTAR's project (C68) is a separate rate track from DNR's lease decision.
